scenes.tts: If height is highly heritable, does that tell you how much of your own height came from genes? No. Heritability describes differences across a population, so our picture begins with many people.
scenes.caption: If height is highly heritable, does that tell you how much of your own height came from genes? No. Heritability describes differences across a population, so our picture begins with many people.
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP for both films: BLUE = measured genetic differences and tag SNPs; GREY = environment or context; GOLD = question or candidate cause; GREEN = converging functional evidence; RED = confounding or reduced portability. Open on one large person silhouette filling the frame beside the GOLD question. The silhouette shrinks as a crowd flows in from both sides. Keep the crowd gently shifting while narration continues. Label the picture 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: If height is highly heritable, does that tell you how much of your own height came from genes? No. Heritability describes differences across a population, so our picture begins with many people.

scenes.visual: Over the carried crowd, show the title 'Heritability Is About Variation' for two seconds, then transform the letters into the baseline of a histogram.

scenes.tts: Each person inherits many alleles by Mendel's rules. Give each small-effect allele a blue tile, then stack the tiles beneath each person. Few people collect only low or high stacks. Most gather combinations near the middle. With more loci, the classes multiply and sit closer together, although every allele remains discrete.

scenes.visual: Blue allele tiles descend into stacks beneath six large person silhouettes. The silhouettes slide horizontally according to stack height, then duplicate into histogram bins. Show a small 'schematic' label because effect sizes are simplified. Keep tiles pulsing softly after they settle.
scenes.narration: Each person inherits many alleles by Mendel's rules. Give each small-effect allele a blue tile, then stack the tiles beneath each person. Few people collect only low or high stacks. scenes.tts: Now let environmental differences nudge each person left or right. The separate allele-count columns blur into a continuous, bell-shaped distribution. This curve is computed from many small additive effects, then widened by simulated environmental variation. The picture is a model, not a claim that every effect is equal.

scenes.visual: Grey breeze arrows nudge dots left and right while the histogram transforms into a broad curve. Compute the curve from a fixed additive simulation and label it 'computed simulation'. A thin BLUE curve appears first; a wider GREY-edged curve grows from it. Keep dots drifting along the final curve.

scenes.tts: Variance measures spread around the population mean. We can partition that spread into additive, dominance, interaction, and environmental components. The additive part comes from average allele effects and helps predict resemblance between parents and offspring. The components add cleanly only under the model's stated assumptions.

The additive part comes from average allele effects and helps predict resemblance between parents and offspring. The components add cleanly only under the model's stated assumptions.
scenes.visual: The curve pours into four large labelled containers: additive BLUE, dominance BLUE outline, interaction BLUE dots, and environment GREY. A total-spread bracket expands above them. Use no molecular imagery. Containers gently slosh while named, and place 'simplified model' beneath them.

scenes.tts: Narrow-sense heritability divides additive variance by total phenotypic variance. Broad-sense heritability divides all genetic variance by the same total. These ratios have no units, and both belong to the population being measured. Changing the environment can alter the denominator even when allele frequencies stay the same.
scenes.caption: Narrow-sense heritability divides additive variance by total phenotypic variance. Broad-sense heritability divides all genetic variance by the same total. These ratios have no units, and both belong to the population being measured. Changing the environment can alter the denominator even when allele frequencies stay the same.
scenes.visual: Animate brackets around the additive container and then all three genetic containers, each over the same total bracket. Show formulas only on screen: h² = V_A/V_P and H² = V_G/V_P. The numerator brackets move while the denominator remains fixed; do not show worked values.
scenes.narration: Narrow-sense heritability divides additive variance by total phenotypic variance. Broad-sense heritability divides all genetic variance by the same total. scenes.tts: Keep every genetic tile exactly where it is. Now make the environmental nudges more varied. Will heritability rise, fall, or stay the same?
scenes.caption: Keep every genetic tile exactly where it is. Now make the environmental nudges more varied. Will heritability rise, fall, or stay the same?
scenes.visual: Return to the crowd and freeze every BLUE tile. Grey arrows lengthen and the curve begins widening, then stops halfway. Put the GOLD question above the curve. No answer appears.
scenes.narration: Keep every genetic tile exactly where it is. Now make the environmental nudges more varied. Will heritability rise, fall, or stay the same?

scenes.visual: Hold the GOLD question and frozen BLUE tiles. Let only the grey environmental arrows breathe slowly during the deliberate thinking pause.

scenes.tts: The total spread grows while the genetic variance stays the same, so heritability falls. Reverse the change, and heritability rises without any DNA changing. A ratio changes when one part changes and the other does not.
scenes.caption: The total spread grows while the genetic variance stays the same, so heritability falls. Reverse the change, and heritability rises without any DNA changing. A ratio changes when one part changes and the other does not.
scenes.visual: Complete the widening curve. A ratio gauge moves downward while BLUE genetic spread stays fixed and GREY environmental spread expands. Then briefly reverse the animation and move the gauge upward. Label both curves 'computed simulation'; do not show worked values.
scenes.narration: The total spread grows while the genetic variance stays the same, so heritability falls. Reverse the change, and heritability rises without any DNA changing. A ratio changes when one part changes and the other does not.

scenes.tts: That is why heritability cannot divide one person's height into genetic and environmental percentages. One person has a phenotype, but no population variance. High heritability also does not mean the trait cannot change.
scenes.caption: That is why heritability cannot divide one person's height into genetic and environmental percentages. One person has a phenotype, but no population variance. High heritability also does not mean the trait cannot change.
scenes.visual: The crowd contracts to one person. A proposed BLUE-GREY percentage split appears, then dissolves rather than receiving a harsh rejection mark. The person moves upward as the environment improves, while the label 'heritability' stays attached to the faded crowd behind.
scenes.narration: That is why heritability cannot divide one person's height into genetic and environmental percentages. One person has a phenotype, but no population variance. High heritability also does not mean the trait cannot change.

scenes.tts: The same limit applies between groups. A large genetic share within each group does not explain a difference between their averages. Different environments can shift whole distributions while genetic differences still explain variation within each one.
scenes.caption: The same limit applies between groups. A large genetic share within each group does not explain a difference between their averages. Different environments can shift whole distributions while genetic differences still explain variation within each one.
scenes.visual: Duplicate the computed curve into two trays. Keep identical BLUE within-tray spreads, then slide one entire curve right with a GREY environment arrow. Mark the between-group cause with a GOLD question mark. Label the curves 'schematic analogy'.
scenes.narration: The same limit applies between groups. A large genetic share within each group does not explain a difference between their averages. Different environments can shift whole distributions while genetic differences still explain variation within each one.

scenes.tts: Twin studies estimate variance components by comparing pair similarities. Under their assumptions, the extra similarity of identical twins over fraternal twins reflects half the additive share. Doubling that gap estimates the additive share. The estimate still describes that sampled population and environment.
scenes.caption: Twin studies estimate variance components by comparing pair similarities. scenes.visual: Two large twin-pair cartoons enter over the same population curve. Similarity bands contract by different amounts; the gap between them doubles, then feeds a BLUE additive container. Keep a visible 'assumptions' bracket around equal environments, additive effects, and random mating. Label the drawing 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Twin studies estimate variance components by comparing pair similarities. scenes.tts: Many small Mendelian effects can create smooth variation, but heritability asks only how that variation is partitioned. Keep the scope attached to every estimate.

scenes.visual: Flow backward through the carried world: twin pairs become the crowd, the crowd becomes the computed curve, and the curve settles above the four variance containers. A scope bracket closes around 'population + environment' while all objects continue a subtle breathing motion.

scenes.visual: Clear every object. Show one centered line only: 'Heritability describes variation in a population and environment, never a person.'
